capabilities.why: Snapshots allow the agent to checkpoint the sandbox state before executing a risky or potentially destructive command. If the command triggers a failure at step 7 of 10 or causes irreversible side-effects, the agent can instantly roll back to the pre-risk snapshot instead of crashing and leaving an orphaned machine. This makes failure recovery deterministic and safe.

Safety hooks are Python callbacks that run before each command reaches the guest VM. Unlike a system prompt instruction that the LLM can be tricked into ignoring through prompt injection, a safety hook is enforced at the infrastructure layer and cannot be bypassed by untrusted content. This is the primary mechanism that ensures destructive commands like rm -rf or secret exfiltration attempts are blocked before execution.

Network policy restricts outbound internet access from the guest sandbox, preventing prompt-injected payloads from exfiltrating environment variables or API keys to attacker-controlled servers. By default internet is on; switching it off or to an allowlist ensures that even if the agent is tricked by a poisoned document or webpage, no sensitive data can leave the sandbox boundary.
